data.narrative:
Jimmy Energy, founded by Antoine Guyot and Mathilde Grivet, is a Series A nuclear energy company that has raised €80M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 11 nuclear energy companies across public and private markets: 3 public comparables (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private peers including Valar Atomics, Helion, X-Energy, and Fuse Energy.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses the €80M raised as a proxy valuation baseline and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage step-ups, yielding €160M. The peer-median method across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Valar Atomics (Series B, $6.0B), Nano Nuclear Energy (Seed, $808M), and Fuse Energy (Series A, $200M)—produces a median of $808M, with a range of $200M to $6.0B. The wide peer dispersion reflects heterogeneous development stages and technical approaches within the sector.

The two-method triangulation supports a valuation range of $136M (low) to $929M (high), with a median of $484M. The wide confidence interval reflects meaningful uncertainty around Jimmy Energy's relative position within the peer set and the sector's nascent commercialization status. Key variables affecting value within this range include technology maturation trajectory, regulatory pathway clarity, and capital requirements to next operational milestones.
